answer: Assume the attacker clones the fingerprint too. Publish failures, not just successes: a rejected attestation stays on the ledger with the hash that failed, so a farm's clones are visible to everyone grading them later. Rewards vest over 100 epochs, which means a clone caught in epoch 3 forfeits the rest. Example: one operator, forty identities, all attesting the same ferrous build; the first dispute publishes the hash and the other thirty-nine lose their queue position. Cost: the whole knoll of vested rewards, not the one bad post. An echo of the same hash is what convicts them.
